material: basketball or soccer ball and hand pump
note: one ball and one hand pump with one needle; not a playground ball, which holds too little air to show a clear gain; the teacher alone attaches the needle and pumps until the ball is firm but still dents under a thumb, or to the gauge reading printed on the ball; trial the readings the day before and need a gain of at least 4 g
holds the ball while it is weighed and pumped; wiped at clean-up
worn by the teacher and the children near the pump on day 1 and by every child for the syringes on day 3 (30 pairs, or a rotating set sanitised between groups)

reads whole grams; trial the day before; dry the scale and the outside of anything before weighing; zero it with the tray on it; a household stand-in; day 1 shows the display on a document camera or a child holds a large-number card; day 2 weighs the soil tray; day 4 uses two scales with three groups at each
two scales with three groups at each, so every group weighs in a 3 minute turn; trial both the day before
chart paper with the unit question and the first question, What entered the ball?; children add I-wonder slips on day 1; each day names the question it answers; answers move beside evidence
printed from readiness.md; one child, one sheet; sorted afterward for gap M and gap P
cut from cereal-box card at no cost, from readiness-pieces.md; six in an envelope for each child, the same six used again on day 2
the day 1 air drawing, dated and never erased; day 3 and day 4 revisions go beside it
printed from the exit rows; four minutes; read aloud when needed
one row for each child; the teacher keeps it; readiness M and P, the exit ticks and the error letters go here
English and Spanish; nothing comes back to school
invented for practice, not an observation: a flat and a pumped ball on one scale; used only in a room with no ball, pump or scale
six for each group of five, counted back to six at clean-up; a household stand-in

material: two books and a small eraser
note: for each pair with gap P: a card piece across two books, flat then folded, to see which holds the eraser

material: unfertilised seed-starting mix or bagged topsoil
note: a cup for each group; check plant and mold allergies first; keep it in trays on a towel; clean up with a damp towel, never a brush; children with asthma stand back and a mask is offered; the teacher handles it if needed
soil spread thin on a labelled, dated tray on day 2; it dries for two school days before day 4
wipes soil off tables and trays instead of sweeping; no dust
soap and towels; hands are washed after soil on days 2 and 4 and after chalk on day 3
invented for practice, not an observation: six numbered blocks as a bridge and then a wall; used only when blocks are missing

one for each group of five, tip closed with a cap or a clean gloved finger; the teacher checks before class that the cap will not pop off under a gentle press; never a needle and never aimed at a face
printed from dot-panels.md; paper dots to count and draw on; they stand in for the viewer, which is spec only

six sticks of one height, a metre long, each upright in a labelled tub of sand set on a marked spot, one for each group; each spot is marked with a paint pen or nail and photographed; put back on the same spot each month
labels the tubs and spots for the day; the lasting mark is made with a paint pen or nail
makes the lasting mark for each stick tub before class; photograph each mark
reads the shadow in centimeters from the mark at the foot of the stick to the tip of the shadow
printed from shadow-record.md; one reading a month at the same clock time as today; units 2 and 4 reuse it
invented for practice, not an observation: air in a closed syringe at two volumes and a first shadow; used only when no syringe is at hand
a labelled pot for each group of five, without holes or standing in a saucer or tray; unit 2 reuses them

four untreated grocery beans (or two large lima beans) for each pot so the line reads 2 g or more; check the packaging and leave out treated garden seed; check for food allergies, especially legumes; never eat the beans
weighed in grams as it is added; each addition has its own line

material: capped plastic bottle with only air in it
note: a capped bottle that gives a little when squeezed; it holds air, so it is not empty; the teacher squeezes it for the class
printed from pot-log.md; dry soil, beans and water each on their own line, in grams
invented for practice, not an observation: an empty pot, dry soil, seeds and added water in grams; used when the soil is not dry
